title: Lessons from L.A. on Transfer Taxes
gist: RAND economist Jason Ward uses his Measure ULA research to warn San Francisco about its new Prop I: L.A.'s price-based transfer tax raised $1.4B vs. $1.8–3.5B projected, cut multifamily sales 47% and large-apartment construction at least 30%, costing ~$500M in revenue; first-sale exemptions help but rigid earmarks magnify affordable-housing funding problems.

themes.theme: San Francisco's new Prop I and outlook

insights.claim: San Francisco's new Prop I would earmark half of future transfer tax proceeds for affordable housing and tenant aid, add a five-year exemption on the first sale of new multifamily properties, and remove the Board of Supervisors' ability to amend the tax, making the earmark permanent.

insights.so_what: Locking in the tax structure removes a future lever for rate relief on SF real estate.
